text.p: Italian debt futures closed almost unchanged from Thursday after a choppy ride, spiking upwards when U.S. data showed a surprise drop in payroll jobs before slumping as hedge funds took profits, some of them reportedly switching into bunds.
The LIFFE December BTP contract leaped to the day's high of 123.70 on the payroll news then tumbled quickly as the profit-taking set in before staging a small rally at the close.
"I would not rush in to buy Italy at these levels," said a London futures trader. "This is a dangerous market to be in."
But traders said the convergence story was still alive and well but investors wanted to see signs of consolidation before reentering the market.
"Some degree of correction is healthy. Looking at the charts, the market could fall to 122 without injuring the bull run," said another London trader.
Earlier definitive CPI figures showed Italian September inflation fully in line with expectations at 3.4 percent year-on-year.
The market was also unfazed by second quarter GDP figures which showed the economy continuing to stagnate nbut not in recession, ananlysts said.
Chart analysts plot a line of support at 123.74 and below that at 123.25. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
